write_per_keystroke.method: 2000 single-character inserts in the middle of the 20k-char chapter. loro = LoroText::insert + commit (the text event is folded into the paragraph mirror); sqlite = INSERT of the commit's encoded update (subscribe_local_update) into a WAL database with synchronous=NORMAL on the local SSD.

marked_chapter.method: The 20k-char chapter plus 500 entity links (entity:<id>, 300 targets) and 200 bold runs of 2–4 characters. open = ProseDoc::from_snapshot (import, mirror with marks, block-id check), five runs; keystroke = 1000 inserts inside an entity link (each typed character joins the link: ExpandType None, inside the span).

cold_open.method: No window. Import Loro snapshots and build the paragraph mirror (ProseDoc::from_snapshot: import, to_delta, paragraphs with attributes and marks, block-id check). book_import_ms on one thread, as P0-B measured it; book_import_parallel_ms on all cores (median of three), which is how the editor opens the book. Every paragraph now carries a block id (loro-schema v0), which doubles Loro's first to_delta.
